key_insight: A foundation-scale chemical language model trained on natural-product representations captures the structural and biosynthetic 'language' of nature, enabling improved prediction, annotation, and generation of natural compounds for downstream discovery tasks.
problem_solved: Natural products are chemically diverse and under-annotated, making it hard to discover, annotate, and design bioactive molecules using conventional, task-specific models; this work provides a general, transferable model tailored to the unique distributions of natural compounds.
method: Pretrain a transformer-style chemical language model on large corpora of natural-product representations (e.g., SMILES/SELFIES or graph tokens) using self-supervised objectives to learn structural and substructure patterns.
Fine-tune or probe the pretrained model for downstream tasks such as activity prediction, biosynthetic origin annotation, and de novo natural-product-like molecule generation.
Evaluate transferability and representation quality via embedding visualization and benchmark comparisons on multiple NP-focused tasks.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a reusable representation and generative backbone specialized for natural products, accelerating annotation, virtual screening, and biologically plausible molecule design while reducing the need for large labeled datasets.

paper_title: Learning the chemical language of natural products
paper_authors: Xu Guo, Celia M. Rava, Allison S. Walker
